chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from Ismail ibn al-Fad-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the blood-money of the Magians, the Jews, and the Christians: is there anything upon them and upon the one who kills them, when they overcome the Muslims and display enmity to them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is habitual in killing them.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the Muslim: would he be killed due to the People of the Covenant (Zimmi) and the People of the Book, when he kills them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if it happens to be habitual for that, not leaving killing them, so he would be killed due to it, and he would be belittled.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing non-Muslims in Shia fiqh according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance on the blood-money (diyah) and retaliation (qisas) for killing People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) and Magians, distinguishing between general killing and habitual killing. It establishes that while there is no specific penalty for killing them in most cases, a Muslim who habitually kills them is executed and held in low esteem (saghir), reflecting the principle of 'al-waqi‘ fihi' (the one who commits the act). This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the status of non-Muslims under Islamic rule, particularly when they are not in a state of war.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about blood of the Magian, and the Jew, and the Christian, is there anything upon them and upon the one who kills them, when they overcome the Muslims and display enmity to them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except if he is habitual in killing them’.

He (the narrator) said: ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Muslim, would he be killed due to the Zimmy people, and the People of the Book, when he kills them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except if it happens to be habitual for that, not leaving killing them, so he would be killed due to it, and he would be belittled’.
